text:
marta: Heads up — saw a sustained reconnect spike on eu-prod around 11:02. Console shows >3x reconnects and duplicate token billing for a subset of socket clients. :eyes:
kevin: Ugh. Any obvious root cause? proxy or client?
alex: Looking at the proxy logs now. There's a repeating pattern: idle proxy 60s timeout, then client reconnect with resume token -> proxy returns 204 -> client treats as disconnect and retries without resume header. That leads to a full new session allocation and billing.
marta: So resume is getting dropped by proxy on idle?
alex: Looks like it. The proxy removes the resume header when it goes through the keepalive rewrite path. Snippet from proxy trace: `Header: X-Resume-Token -> dropped in rewrite middleware`
kevin: Can we add a quick mitigation by making backend accept a fallback header that indicates "attempt-resume"?
bella: We should be careful — adding new headers affects network/router ACLs and may leak through to customer logs. Product wants a console flag that marks these reconnects as "transient-retry" so billing UI can filter.
nate: +1 for telemetry tag. If we add a new header, we can also add an internal telemetry tag `x-rw-resume-hint: true` so the router annotates metrics and the console can surface a deduped count.
marta: Agree on telemetry. But is header change faster than fixing the proxy rewrite bug?
alex: Fixing rewrite is a 2-patch change (proxy + upstream middleware) and needs canary. Header & telemetry tag is a smaller rollback-safe change we can ship as a feature flag.
kevin: Example header we could use: ```
X-RW-Resume-Hint: resume-safe
```
kevin: Backend will treat requests with that header as idempotent replays for 30s and avoid double-billing.
console-team: If you expose a flag we can add a dashboard panel that shows "reconnects with resume-hint" vs "full-session starts" and a filter to hide resume-safe reconns in billing.
bella: UX note: customers will expect the console to show true cost. Hiding reconns might confuse teams during incident triage. We should surface both but flag deduped costs separately.
marta: Good point. Let's surface a deduped_cost column and keep gross_cost as well.
kevin: For rollout plan: (1) add header + telemetry tagging behind a feature flag (2) console panel work (3) proxy rewrite fix in canary (4) flip flag off when rewrite deployed. Agreed?
nate: Also add a metric: `stream.resume_drop_rate` with tag `proxy_path` so we can track which proxies are rewriting headers.
alex: I'll open the proxy PR with a unit test for header passthrough. ETA EOD for the PR, but canary won't be done until tomorrow.
marta: Who picks up the telemetry+console panel?
console-team: We'll take the panel if you ship the telemetry tag today. We can have an internal beta dashboard by EOD as well.
bella: We should add an alert rule: if ratio of reconnects-to-new-sessions > 2 for >5m, page eng-oncall. Current incident was 15m long.
kevin: Deploy-bot: starting canary rollout of the header flag to eu-edge (10% traffic) now.
deploy-bot: Deploy initiated: feature=rw-resume-hint, target=eu-edge, pct=10, user=kevin, ts=1832111200
alex: Canary looks clean so far in logs; telemetry comes through with `resume_hint=true`. I can wire the metric to the console panel's data source.
console-team: Panel wired. Showing timestamped spikes and the deduped_cost column. Leaving comment in dashboard for product review.
bella: Product asked whether we can auto-detect when resume_hint is unnecessary. Maybe after proxy fix we want to stop setting it. Plan for automated TTL: set hint header only if previous session ended within 30s.
marta: Ok, action items: Alex PR for proxy fix (blocker remediation), Kevin rollout header flag (mitigation), Nate add metric and tag, Console-team add panel, Bella coordinate product message.
kevin: I'll also add a telemetry sample in the request logs: `resume_hint=1` and `resume_result=accepted|failed` for better tracing.
nate: I'm adding `stream.resume_drop_rate` alert now.
alex: PR: https://git.internal/r/proxy/merge/789 (WIP) — includes passthrough test.
marta: Thanks. Let's regroup after canary stabilizes. If the deduped billing numbers stay high after proxy fix we may need to retroactively credit customers. :thinking_face:
